# Unversioned disposable prototype

Research fixture only; do not run these files against a hosted database. The caller-settable `forms.pilot_fixture` marker is an accident guard, not a security boundary. No real approval row or real identity is included. The synthetic HTTP script accepts only a disposable loopback endpoint and uses a public test JWT key.

The SQL replaces existing function bodies and preserves their existing ACLs, introduces an empty owner/site gate, and locks the gate and website during guarded operations. Rollback restores the exact local source bodies and eight held ACLs for the synthetic baseline. Neither file is a production migration or hosted rollback: target identities, dependencies, inherited privileges, runner atomicity, rollout and unknown outcomes require separate review. Revocation denies even existing same-ID retries until approval returns; responses and idempotency data remain intact. Public owner reads remain governed by their existing RLS and are not pilot-filtered.

For local PGlite run `node --test supabase/tests/forms-pilot-scope.test.mjs`. The PostgREST fixture requires a freshly initialized disposable PostgreSQL and PostgREST with roles and HTP migrations 000–009 and quota 28, the eight held ACLs, the prototype and `seed.sql` (both set the local fixture marker in their SQL session). Configure PostgREST with the synthetic key in `postgrest-check.mjs`. `PILOT_FIXTURE=disposable PILOT_FIXTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ node supabase/tests/fixtures/forms-pilot-scope/postgrest-check.mjs` checks held access; after a disposable regrant of begin/challenge/save/status only, set `PILOT_FIXTURE_PHASE=open` to check owner/site isolation and retry. These checks do not prove hosted behavior.
